problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{x}-3xy,\,y(-2)=3
$$

The **implicit** Euler method is applied with step size $Δx=1.$ 
Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and the current value $y.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4{x}^{2}-5{x}^{2}y,\,y(1)=0
$$

The **implicit** Euler method is applied with step size $Δx=\frac{1}{5}.$ 
Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and the current value $y.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(4{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot \frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{4}{5}{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{4}{5}{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}) & =y+\frac{4}{5}{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ 5{y}_{\text{new}}(1+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}) & =5y+4{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(5+5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}) & =5y+4{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5y+4{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}}{5+5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
